Class SsList1<K,D>

java.lang.Object
java.awt.Component
java.awt.Container
javax.swing.JComponent
javax.swing.JList<ListItem>
dev.visdb.seesaw.SsList1<K,D>
Type Parameters:
K -
D -
All Implemented Interfaces:
RSC, SsComponent, ImageObserver, MenuContainer, Serializable, Accessible, Scrollable
public class SsList1<K,D> extends JList<ListItem> implements SsComponent
Provides a way to display a list of elements and map them to corresponding database keys. These keys are typically provided by setDisplayValues method; if param keys are null they default to zero to N-1. The keys for the selected JList values are typically in a DB as controlled by a DbCollection; if not specified DbArray is used by default and this model saves the selected keys in a column of type JDBCType.ARRAY. 
  /**
   * Create an SsList1, initialize its contents,
bind the list selection to a column in the RowsModel.
   */
  @SuppressWarnings("unused")
  void init() {
    list = new SsList1<>(JDBCType.DOUBLE);
    List<String> options = List.of("VLarge", "large", "medium", "small", "VSmall");
    List<Object> mappings = List.of(100.0, 10.0, 5.0, 1.0, 0.1);
    list.setDisplayValues(options, mappings);
    rowsModel.bind(list, "my_column");
  }
From the example above, if three values VLarge, medium, small are selected the array element in the database will store {100.0,5.0,1.0}

    • setDisplayValues

      public void setDisplayValues(List<D> displayValues, List<K> keys)
      Sets the displayValues to be displayed in the list box along with their corresponding keys to database values. If keys is null, then zero to N-1 keys are automatically established.

      If keys is null, then autogenerate the keys; keys type must be Integer or Long.

      Parameters:
      displayValues - displayed in the list box.
      keys - null or database values that correspond to the displayValues, 1 to 1, in the list box.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if lists are not the same size.
